description: We are developing a fast and efficient system to combine MODIS and VIIRS satellite data into a single, unified map of thermal anomalies. By treating the satellite feeds as raw telemetry, we use a custom low-level processing engine to align the data perfectly in space and time. Our solution automatically resolves the differences in sensor resolutions and observation schedules, delivering a clean, optimized dataset of active fires that is ready for instant AI analysis and real-time monitoring.
summary: TELETRAAN-1 is a global wildfire analysis web app that turns NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS detections into an interactive burning activity calendar. Users can compare raw and harmonized records from 2000 to 2025, explore hotspots on a 3D map, and export reports and GIS data. Historical fire recurrence zones help land managers and planners identify locations that warrant closer investigation.
details:
TELETRAAN-1 addresses the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.” It brings NASA FIRMS detections from Terra and Aqua MODIS and Suomi NPP VIIRS into one workspace for exploring where and when burning activity was recorded.

Users select a country, administrative region, ecoregion, or custom area, then filter by date and daytime or nighttime satellite pass. The calendar displays weekly hotspot counts, fire radiative power (FRP), or seasonal Z-scores. Users can open a week to inspect individual days and compare Raw Satellite and Harmonized views. Harmonization applies pass-specific calibration to earlier MODIS observations to make comparisons across the transition to VIIRS more meaningful.

On the map, users can tilt the view to see FRP as 3D columns, switch to satellite imagery, measure distances to nearby infrastructure, and save their settings as pins. A separate historical fire zones layer highlights clusters with recurring MODIS detections. Planners can use these polygons to flag candidate sites for further assessment and prioritize where to investigate.

TELETRAAN-1 exports filtered CSV, GeoJSON for GIS, statistical PDF reports, and supporting JSON evidence. The application uses React, TypeScript, Kepler.gl, and MapLibre for the interface, with Python, FastAPI, and DuckDB for queries over a local Parquet archive. Our goal is to make historical satellite observations easier to compare, interpret, and use in land management and planning.

dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) provides the archived Terra MODIS, Aqua MODIS, and Suomi NPP VIIRS active-fire hotspot records used in the calendar, map, harmonization, and reports. We use detection time, location, sensor identity, and fire radiative power (FRP) when available.
NASA EOSDIS GIBS provides satellite imagery layers used to put the geographic selection and detection records in context.
NASA Earth Observatory Blue Marble imagery provides the Earth texture used in the orbital view. NASA Goddard's CGI Moon Kit provides the Moon texture.

Software: Python, FastAPI, DuckDB, Apache Parquet, React, TypeScript, Vite, and Kepler.gl. The repository documents the implementation, additional software dependencies, and asset credits.
